## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to bridge C callbacks into Go in a streaming, multi-chunk workflow, focusing on memory ownership and error propagation across boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- CGO callback bridging and opaque context handles
- Memory ownership and cross-language malloc/free
- Streaming guarantees and error propagation
- Concurrency safety with channels and worker pools

## Code Example
```c
// header sketch
int stream_pca_all(const double** blocks, const size_t* lengths, size_t n, void (*on_result)(const char* json_chunk, void* ctx), void* ctx);
```
```go
// binding sketch: StreamPCA(blocks [][]float64) (string, error)
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test memory ownership and guard against leaks in streaming mode?
- How would you ensure chunk order guarantees if C delivers out-of-order chunks?
- How would cancellation and timeouts be wired across Go and C boundaries?
